open_project.description: Create or reopen the PPTD project bound to this DSH session. Do not pass a filesystem path.

inspect_capabilities.description: List vision, search, render, and export capabilities that are actually configured. Do not invent a capability. Hub chips and this tool are the same snapshot.

list_references.description: Check required source-chunk status on demand, not every turn. Without filters, returns compact referencesComplete, requiredReferenceChunks, missingReferenceChunks, next, counts and family/kind totals, with no catalog rows. For a directory, pass family or kind; optional tag narrows the listing. Filtered rows contain only sourceId, kind and chunks. Read every required chunk before commit_design/write_todo. Filters affect only the catalog listing, never the required preflight.

family.description: Optional family from familyTotals, such as academic, consulting or general

read_reference.description: Read one OpenKimi source or section chunk (for example openkimi:reference/pptd.md::chart) by sourceId and chunkIndex. Marks the source consulted.

list_materials.description: List the user's uploaded reference materials (图片、表格、文档、PPT 模板) with recognized summaries and readable parts. PPT templates expose design, layouts, slides, tables and charts with UTF-8 byte sizes and chunk counts; smartart appears only when diagrams exist; kit appears only when the template has reusable decoration components. Images list palette; a PDF lists document and palette, its page-image count, and tables when table structure was reconstructed. A Word or Excel file lists charts when the file carries embedded charts. Call this first, then read every part you rely on through read_material before using its facts. Place user images via mediaSrc.

read_material.description: Read one part of an uploaded material by materialId. For PPT templates, design contains observed colors and actually used fonts; layouts gives descriptive position/use cues; slides returns per-slide text including SmartArt trees; tables and charts preserve extracted values; smartart returns per-diagram text summaries and exists only when present; kit lists the template's reusable components as material:<id>#<componentId> references with role, archetype, box and scopeHint (layout or page), which the Host expands where they are written into a page (or into a layout, in turns that edit layouts) once the template's decorations or photos use is declared and the whole kit part has been read. Template chunks are ≤12 KiB UTF-8, slides/charts/tables carry `## 第 N 页` headings, and chart types PPTD cannot draw are marked as unsupported. Documents return ordered markdown chunks (offset = chunk index, 0-based); a PDF's part tables returns its reconstructed tables as markdown per page (自动识别，可能有错位) or a Chinese empty note; tables return the header plus data rows in at most 12 KiB of UTF-8 text (offset = zero-based data row, limit ≤ 200, with absolute row indices). A window may return fewer rows than limit; when hasMore is true, continue with offset = rows.endIndex, not offset + limit. An oversized single row is explicitly marked and truncated = true; oversized headers may also be shortened. Any row of a large CSV/XLSX is reachable by its absolute offset; images return metadata and their measured palette (part palette), and a PDF's part palette merges its vector and page-pixel colours — read it before adopting that image or PDF for palette. Exact values only — never invent numbers or text that a part did not return.

part.description: Optional part id from list_materials. PPT templates: design, layouts, slides, tables, charts, or smartart / kit when listed; images and PDFs: palette; PDFs also list tables when detected; Word and Excel list charts when the file carries embedded charts (cached values usable for a native write_page chart); other examples: sheet:明细, document, rows.

offset.description: Chunk index (documents) or zero-based data row (tables); default 0

limit.description: Max data rows (≤200); the 12 KiB UTF-8 bound may return fewer; ignored for documents

query_material.description: Compute exact numbers from an uploaded CSV/XLSX table (read-only, deterministic, no formulas). Pipeline: filter [{column, op: "="|"!="|">"|"<"|"in"|"contains", value}] → groupBy [columns] → measures [{op: sum|count|avg|min|max, column (omit for a plain count), as}] → derive [{as, op: share|yoy|mom|ratio|diff|unit, of, base?, factor?}] over measure/derive aliases (share = value / column total of all groups, yoy and mom = (of − base) / base, ratio = of / base, diff = of − base, unit = of × factor) → sort [{by, dir: asc|desc}] → limit (≤ 200). Column names must match the header exactly; part is "rows" for CSV or "sheet:<name>" for XLSX (required when the workbook has several sheets). Returns cols, rows, notes and a receipt (material and result hashes, row counts). An empty or zero base gives null plus a note, never a guess. Every computed number on a page (sums, shares, 同比, 环比, differences) must come from this tool; show values with at most two decimals and fractions (share, yoy, mom) as percentages. Never add up, average or divide table numbers yourself.

filter.description: Row filters, all must hold: {column, op, value}; in takes an array

measures.description: Aggregates: {op, column?, as}; at least one

derive.description: Derived columns: {as, op, of, base?, factor?}

limit.description: Keep the first N result rows (≤ 200)

view_material.description: View uploaded visual material as one normalized JPEG image block (at most 1568 px). Shapes: {materialId} on an image; {materialId:"all-images"} for one numbered mosaic of every session image (template photos included) plus a table from number to material; {materialId} on a PDF for a numbered mosaic of up to 12 rendered pages; {materialId, page} for one PDF page (only the first 40 pages have images; list_materials lists the rendered pages); {materialId, mediaId} for a deck-template photo (the :grayscale id selects the desaturated copy). Only available when the selected model accepts image input (inspect_capabilities.vision.modelAcceptsImages); read_material covers text for every model. After looking, write the conclusion with record_material_notes.

materialId.description: Image, PDF or deck-template material id from list_materials, or "all-images" for the numbered overview of every image

mediaId.description: Template photo mediaId from list_materials; omit for standalone images

page.description: PDF page number (1-based, at most 40 rendered pages); required to view a PDF page image

record_material_notes.description: Record what you concluded from an image you viewed, so its picture can later be replaced by this text. Target: {materialId} for an image; {materialId, mediaId} for a deck-template photo; {materialId, page} for a PDF page. caption (required): one or two sentences about what the picture shows. suggestedUse (required): "page" (place it on a slide), "background", "logo", "style-reference" (only learn from its look) or "skip". Optional: focus [x, y] (0–1, the subject's position for cropping), layoutNotes, mood, fontClass ("sans"|"serif"|"kai"|"mono": a class, never a font name; the Host maps it to whitelisted fonts), readValues [{label, value, unit?, period?}] for numbers you read off the picture (shown to the user as unverified), reason. Only available when the selected model accepts image input.

readValues.description: Numbers read from the picture: [{label, value, unit?, period?}]

commit_design.description: Commit the slide plan after list_references reports referencesComplete=true. Pass ordered {pageId, title, layoutFamily, exhibits}[] including a valid single-page plan. Plan items may carry an optional layoutId naming the page's layout. adoptedSourceIds selects ordered visual sources; designAspects declares each source's uses from the user's own words. userColors lists colours the user named, so the page palette checks accept them. Content/data do not require visual adoption but require complete current-epoch part reads. Adopt palette/fonts only when requested; logo-only adoption never changes theme colors or fonts. Put the main brand first. designAuthority names the effective style (catalog pack, material:<id>, or hub-choice) with the user's own words or the exact current answer; it replaces the Hub style as authority, never becomes a catalog designSystemId, and grants no page or layout permission. Host never imports source pages or classifies adoption from brief keywords. Do not invent a host preset id. Plan every page the brief needs.

slidePlan.description: Complete ordered plan: {pageId, title, layoutFamily, exhibits, note?, purpose?, layoutId?}. layoutId names the page layout the page is planned to use. Use an explicit empty exhibits array when none are needed. One page is valid.

adoptedSourceIds.description: Canonical array of source ids actually adopted.

designAspects.description: Per-source uses, e.g. [{source:"material:brand.pptx",aspects:["palette","fonts","logo"]}]. Allowed: palette, fonts, logo, layouts, decorations, photos, content, data. Declare the aspects requested by the user, not a brief keyword guess. Visual uses require adoptedSourceIds and complete current-epoch design reads. Content requires slides reads; data requires charts or tables reads, without visual adoption. Omitted adopted PPTX entries default to palette/fonts/logo for compatibility. Omitted field on plan updates retains the current declaration. An image, logo or screenshot accepts only palette; a PDF accepts palette (not under a Hub style pack), content and data; both require the read_material palette part first.

userColors.description: Colours the user named in their own message (a hex value, a colour word or a brand colour), e.g. [{hex:'#1F4E9A', reason:'用户要求主色换成蓝色'}]. hex is #RRGGBB; reason names what the user asked. They are allowed on page and layout elements in addition to the selected style pack, adopted template or image palette, with the same tints and shades. Colours that come from attachments, templates, images or style packs are never userColors: they become allowed by adopting that source with the palette aspect, or are already allowed by the selected style pack or an adopted template. Leave this field out when the user named no colour. The Host never reads colours from the brief and never changes the theme for you. Omitted keeps the earlier list, [] clears it.

reportRequirements.description: Requirements this plan enforces: [{id, role, statement, origin, material?}]. role: content-source | explicit-requirement | design-reference. Only explicit-requirement is mandatory, and its origin must be {kind:"user-request"} or {kind:"clarification-answer", questionId, text} quoting the actual answer to that question in the current conversation. Attachment prose never grants itself authority. material links the requirement to what it truly depends on: an explicit rule that constrains source pages depends on that material's slides part; layout/table/chart/component work names the matching part. Only declared dependencies are required, and current-epoch read_material receipts must cover them. Omitted keeps the earlier declaration; [] clears it.

designAuthority.description: The style that governs this plan now: {source, origin:{kind, questionId?, text}}. source is a catalog pack id, "material:<id>" for an adopted attachment, or "hub-choice" to keep the Hub style. origin.text quotes the user's own request or the exact answer to that current-conversation question; kind:"clarification-answer" also needs that questionId. The Host refuses an attachment that authorized itself, a source this plan does not adopt, a cancelled/interrupted/expired/older answer, and an unknown pack. Declaring another source replaces the Hub style as the effective authority while the original designSystemId stays as history; an attachment never becomes a catalog designSystemId. A material source also needs a visual aspect in designAspects. Omitted keeps the saved decision. This changes no page, element or layout permission.

write_todo.description: Commit the page plan after list_references reports referencesComplete=true. Same plan shape as commit_design: items [{pageId, title, layoutFamily, exhibits}]. Plan items may carry an optional layoutId naming the page's layout. A single-page task is valid. Returns notInPlan and non-blocking hints for orphan pages and differing explicit page counts. Restore orphan ids to the plan or call delete_pages before compose. A rejected preflight leaves the plan unchanged. adoptedSourceIds, per-source designAspects, designAuthority and userColors follow commit_design; omit them to retain the current selection, uses, style decision and colours. Plan every page the brief needs. Uploaded images: put each image id on the page that shows it in items[].materials; declare the rest in materialUse. Updating last month's deck with new data: also pass periodMap, and missingItems for template charts or tables with no new data.

items.description: Complete ordered plan: {pageId, title, layoutFamily, exhibits, note?, purpose?, layoutId?}. layoutId names the page layout the page is planned to use. Use an explicit empty exhibits array when none are needed. One page is valid.

materials.description: Uploaded image ids (list_materials ids) this page shows; images only.

materialUse.description: Per uploaded image: [{materialId, use, reason}]. use: placed | background | logo | style-reference | excluded. excluded needs a reason the user can read; a style-reference image needs no page; images in items[].materials need an entry only for background or logo. Omitted keeps the earlier declaration, [] clears it. Every uploaded image should end on a page, as a style-reference, or excluded with a reason.

periodMap.description: Monthly update: {from, to}. from is the period last month's deck covers, to is the period this deck covers, e.g. {from:'2026年8月', to:'2026年9月'} or '2026-08' to '2026-09'. With it the Host flags numbers copied from last month's charts and tables (a non-blocking hint). Omitted keeps the earlier map.

missingItems.description: Template charts or tables you have no new-period data for, the whole item or only some of its data points (blank cells in the new data table): [{page, title}], page and title as read_material lists them in the charts or tables part (optional materialId). Needs periodMap and that part read completely. The Host verifies each item and shows it on the delivery card as having no data for this period. Omitted keeps the earlier list, [] clears it.

adoptedSourceIds.description: Canonical array of source ids actually adopted. Use material:<id> for an attached PPTX whose palette, fonts, logo, or layout the user wants, or for an image, logo or screenshot (and, without a Hub style pack, a PDF) whose colours the user wants: declare palette for it and read its palette part first.

read_page.description: Read one current persisted PPTD v2 page by pageId. Strictly read-only: returns the COMPLETE page body plus stable pageSha256 as the baseline before a whole-page write_page edit. Call this immediately before editing an existing page so human changes are preserved.

pageId.description: Existing PPTD page id to read

edit_elements.description: Replace exactly the selected elements in an active editor element review. Pass only the authorized target elements, but each must be one COMPLETE canonical native PPTD element with its existing elementId. The Host reads the current authoritative page, preserves every other element, page metadata, and element order, then executes the same canonical write_page persistence path. Call read_page immediately before this tool and pass its current pageSha256 as expectedPageSha256. Do not wrap arguments or send aliases. When replacing a picture, resend the element with only src changed (keep bounds, fit, crop and cropShape exactly as read_page returned them); when updating a chart from a table, replace only data.rows with the table's numbers and keep its series, grouping and colors. This tool is unavailable outside a live server-verified elements scope.

pageId.description: Existing PPTD page id. Must match the active editor element scope.

elementId.description: Stable id unique within the page.

bounds.description: Exactly [x,y,width,height]; all values finite and width/height positive.

blur.description: Blur radius in PPTD px; zero or more.

opacity.description: Shadow opacity from 0 to 1; it multiplies the alpha of the colour.

shadow.description: Element shadow in PPTD px. Omitted blur, offsetX and offsetY take 12, 0 and 4.

text.description: Plain or rich-text HTML string. Quote numeric labels too: "1", "2", "3". Inline CSS belongs only inside this string.

style.description: Theme text-style reference such as $title. Never pass a style object here.

fontSize.description: Font size belongs directly on content.

oneOf.description: Only a common Office face: 微软雅黑, 黑体, 宋体, 楷体, 仿宋, Arial, Times New Roman, Georgia, Verdana, Tahoma, Courier New. Any other name is rewritten to the closest one and reported back.

latin.description: Latin face from the same list.

ea.description: East Asian face from the same list.

field.description: pageNumber shows the page's own number: {page} becomes its 1-based position and {pages} the deck total. Never zero-pad the tokens.

elements.description: Complete replacements for exactly the authorized target elementIds.

edit_page_background.description: Change ONLY an existing page background. Use this for background-only edits instead of copying all elements into write_page. Pass pageId, expectedPageSha256 from read_page, and the complete canonical background. The Host preserves every element, text string, style, order, notes and animation verbatim. Available only inside an active editor page/deck scope; stale hashes and element-only scopes are rejected. The same write/render and review gates apply.

angle.description: Degrees clockwise, 0 is left to right. Leaving it out resets it to 0.

mode.description: stretch (default) draws the picture once across the shape; tile repeats it at natural size.

batch_remove_footers.description: Batch-remove footer elements (layoutRole=footer, footer* elementIds, or bottom footer-zone page numbers and small footnotes) across all persisted pages or a named pageIds subset, optionally including masters and layouts (includeLayouts defaults to true). Preserves body text, titles, charts, and tables, and fails closed under restricted editor review locks. Prefer this tool over rewriting every page when removing footers.

delete_pages.description: During generation, remove only notInPlan pages authored by this run's agent; planned pages and externally changed pages are refused. In editor turns, remove exactly the pages named by the active structural authorization (deletablePageIds), or the rewrite baseline. For a merge, first write the merged content into the surviving editable page. The page list and manifest update atomically; editor verify rolls back results outside its authorized set.

reorder_pages.description: Reorder the deck's pages to exactly the authorized final order (reorderPageIds). pageIds must list every existing page once, in the authorized sequence. It changes the manifest order only — no page content is rewritten. Verify rolls everything back if the result differs from the authorized order.

update_deck.description: Change deck-level metadata: the presentation title and/or theme. Only the fields named by the active editor authorization (editableMeta) may be sent — a field outside that whitelist is rejected. Page content and the manifest are untouched. A rewrite lock authorizes both fields. Theme textStyles fontFamily uses the same Office/WPS faces as write_page; an off-list face is rewritten and reported in fontNotes.

write_page.description: Write one COMPLETE PPTD v2 page in one call. Host accepts only one write_page at a time: wait for this result before the next page. This is whole-page replacement, never element append: every call must include the full elements[] array. Never omit elements — a background-only page is rejected; a photo cover still carries its title and subtitle as elements above the background. Elements use elementId, elementType, bounds [x,y,w,h], and content.text. First-write layout gate (960x540 slide px): keep every element inside the slide; text boxes never overlap; leave >= 14px between a rule/line and the text below it; text contrast against its fill or background >= 4.5:1 (3:1 at >= 24px or bold >= 18.66px). Text fontSize/fontFamily/color/alignment fields belong directly on content; content.style is only a string theme reference such as $title, never an object. fontFamily must be one of 微软雅黑, 黑体, 宋体, 楷体, 仿宋, Arial, Times New Roman, Georgia, Verdana, Tahoma, Courier New; any other face is rewritten to the closest one and the result lists fontNotes. Prefer {latin, ea} so Latin and Chinese are named separately. layoutRole belongs on the element. Chart elements take series[].type bar, line, area, pie, doughnut, radar, scatter or waterfall (bar and line series may combine); the optional chart grouping is clustered (default), stacked or percentStacked and applies to bar charts only (a stacked bar is type bar with grouping stacked, never a series type). radar needs at least 3 categories; doughnut takes one series with no negative values. Put element fill/line fields inside the owning element; optional page-level metadata is background, notes, and animations. Editing uses the same page id. Treat the complete page from read_page as the baseline, preserve its background/notes/animations, and pass its pageSha256 as expectedPageSha256; an editor review lock rejects stale edits. layoutStatus=pass is overflow-only, not a rewrite seal. The same pageId may be rewritten until review_pages records a current structural pass for that revision. After structural pass, rewrite only if the current revision has explicit editor edit authorization, review_pages names the page failing, or review_page says revise. An authorized editor edit uses read_page and expectedPageSha256; do not manufacture a visual review to enable it. Optional provenance {basis material|mock|mixed|own, materials, quoted, note} records where this page's figures come from; it is stored in the run ledger, never in the page file, and a quoted value that is not in the chunks read this session, or a material figure relabelled with a different period, returns a non-blocking Chinese hint. elements must be a JSON array, not a JSON-encoded string. A page with a layoutId inherits that layout's elements; never redraw one of them on the page. A template component may stand in for a decoration group: an element {elementType:"component", ref:"material:<id>#<componentId>", bounds:[x,y,w,h]} copied from the template's read_material part kit (read it fully first; the template needs the decorations or photos use declared in commit_design). The Host expands it into native elements; it never creates a page, and the page's own text is still written by you. A SmartArt component (its kit entry says smartart) is page-only and may also carry texts: one entry per node in reading order — an entry is the node text or a list of its paragraphs (the first paragraph is the main line). A process component re-lays out evenly to the entry count; every other kind must match its node count exactly. The expansion is ordinary shapes, so the export carries no diagram part.

write_layout.description: Define the deck master (scope master, id main) or one page layout (scope layout) in one call. Use a layout for chrome that repeats on several pages: header line, logo, page number, footer or background. Put that chrome on the layout whose pages show it: every layout inherits the master's elements unless showMasterElements is false. Define the deck master first, then each layout, then write the pages. Page numbers: a text element with content.field pageNumber whose text is {page} (or {pages} for the total); never zero-pad it. Whole replacement: send every element. A page whose layoutId names this layout inherits its elements, so never redraw them on the page. Text, shape, image, line and icon elements only, plus a template component reference {elementType:"component", ref:"material:<id>#<componentId>", bounds:[x,y,w,h]} from the template's read_material part kit (read it fully first; the template needs the decorations use declared in commit_design), which the Host expands into native elements. SmartArt components are page-only: write_layout refuses them, exactly like chart and table elements. An identical definition returns skipped-identical. The outcome lists pagesUsing and pagesNeedingRender; re-render those pages. Master and layout text is generic chrome: a template sample's titles, report names, dates and figures never belong there, and write_layout refuses such text; sample wording goes on pages only.

elements.description: Complete layout elements: text, shape, image, line or icon, at most 40, or a template component reference (elementType component). No chart, table or SmartArt.

slots.description: Reference positions for the layout; slots are never painted.

expectedLayoutSha256.description: layoutSha256 from the last write_layout for this layout; a stale value is refused.

render_page.description: Raster the current page through the native editor #slide screenshot. Host accepts only one render_page at a time: wait for this result before the next page. Wait for this tool result before review_page. When inspect_capabilities.vision.mode is main-model, the PNG is attached as an image part for the selected vision-capable model. Copy the complete DELIVERY_TOKEN from this successful result into review_page for the same pageId and revision.

review_page.description: Aesthetics-only visual review after a successful render_page for this exact pageId and revision. Host accepts only one review_page at a time: wait for this result before the next page. Copy its complete DELIVERY_TOKEN exactly; do not shorten or reuse it. verdict=pass requires issues=[] because praise is not an unresolved issue. verdict=revise requires one or more concrete visible defects in issues. When vision.mode is none this tool is unavailable; use review_pages for deterministic checks and authorized editor edits for human-requested revisions.

review_pages.description: Run deterministic structural and latest-plan coverage review from disk. Missing and extra pages are issues with ok=false and a Chinese recovery hint. Repair missing pages; restore orphan ids to the plan or delete_pages, then review again.

compose_deck.description: Seal current PPTD pages after every required gate passes. Pass only the title. Success returns page IDs, titles, deck hash and a short per-page provenance summary; use read_page for content. On rejection, follow payload.next and the exact missingReferenceChunks/page-id arrays; do not repeat compose_deck without satisfying that step.

web_search.description: Search the web for current information. Provide 1–4 queries in the required queries array. Use a one-item array for a single search. Returns facts and source URLs. First-class produce tool via xAI when inspect_capabilities.research.configured. Assistant prose is not a search.

queries.description: Required search queries; accepts 1–4 items and merges their results.

search_image.description: Search a unique image into media/ when inspect_capabilities.imageSearch.configured. Call this in a batch for every photo-led page (cover, section, closer, body photo) BEFORE write_page. Do not reuse one cover file on later pages. Assistant prose is not a search.

generate_image.description: Generate a unique image into media/ via grok-imagine when inspect_capabilities.imageGenerate.configured. Pass the planned photo frame width and height in page pixels (the write_page image bounds). Host maps that slot to the nearest API aspect so the file matches the frame. Call once per photo-led page BEFORE write_page. Do not default to 16:9 and cover-crop into a portrait column. Fails closed if the image API cannot run — no placeholder PNG.

width.description: Planned image frame width in page pixels

height.description: Planned image frame height in page pixels

aspect.description: Fallback only if width/height cannot be known: 16:9, 1:1, or 3:4

export_deck.description: Export the current PPTD project to a hybrid editable PPTX. Full-page raster is a failure.

open_in_editor.description: Return the local native editor URL for the bound project so a human can open, inspect and edit the deck. Read-only: it never launches a browser or changes the project.
